items.title: Lou Marini interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 15, 2023
items.q: he saw Dr. John in the hallway and Mac said, “David, come in and play a solo on this tune” you know.

ctx.x: Have you ever done a session that the producer or the engineer has you play like ten, like ten solos and then they chop them up and make one out of it?

Oh they do that a lot. And sometimes with my guidance and sometimes not. Sometimes, but you know it used to be, especially when the Japanese were coming in over a lot in the late 70s and we were doing these sessions. I remember one time there was a tune, and it was a good Japanese keyboard player named Jun Fukamachi — complex stuff. And I played an alto solo and I must have done 30 takes. And they would be, “Lou, nice solo but can you play high notes when you play this place.” And you know, like I’m thinking oh…
Okay I’ve got one more, name this session: [scats Paul Simon’s “Late in the Evening”]

items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: And then I did Saturday Night Live for three years with Marini.

ctx.x: Did you have time during this period to get out and play gigs, or did you even want to?

Yeah. I was still gigging here and there you know, and had a little band with John Tropea, we did weekend stuff here and there. I didn’t have to do that. And then I did Saturday Night Live for three years with Marini. For the first two years I was actually the conductor for ’81 to ’83. And then I played guitar in the band after that for a while. And so I did a whole bunch of different – my career was very eclectic.
That’s a – Saturday Night Live is another kind of pressure I would imagine.
